items.basis: The candidate proposes a biological intervention (biocide and dispersant) to control the biofilm share of clogging but explicitly fails to claim any failure modes for this chemistry class operating in a 32-38 C recirculated loop carrying steel scale particles, leaving the interaction between oxidized organics and particulate unaddressed. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "Known failure modes (claimed by the generator): (none claimed)"

The boundary condition requires dosing inside the existing discharge permit, but continuous 0.3 ppm actinic biocide with weekly 8 ppm dispersant slugs introduces persistent oxidizing residuals into the recirculation blowdown stream without demonstrating that these specific concentrations satisfy the existing permit limits. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "dosing inside the existing discharge permit"
No evidence bundle is held, therefore no internal contradiction between evidence records can be demonstrated. GROUNDED_IN: EVIDENCE (none held)

The candidate predicts total clogging events falling from 2.9 to approximately 1.4 per campaign, which is a quantified reduction against the baseline status quo doing nothing new. GROUNDED_IN: COMPUTATION 2.9 baseline events versus 1.4 predicted events

Installing a dosing skid on an existing recirculation loop with ORP control does not contradict the stated boundary condition of no mill stop, as tie-ins can be executed during scheduled downtime or via hot-tap methods consistent with the constraint. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "no mill stop"

The testable prediction relies on monthly header-wall swab cultures showing a 2-order CFU reduction, but header-wall swabs sample the supply pipe surface rather than the internal geometry of the 120 flat-fan spray nozzles where the actual clogging failure occurs, creating a spatial mismatch between the measurement proxy and the failure site. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "monthly header-wall swab cultures show a 2-order CFU reduction" compared to RECORD "progressive nozzle clogging from scale particles and biological growth"
